title: Numina Labs KYC / AML / sanctions checklist
note: Numina Labs is a consulting practice, not a bank or MSB. FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual sections are cited as the reference standard for good practice, not because the bank rules apply directly. Screening aid; not legal advice.

ffiec_bo.section: Beneficial Ownership Requirements for Legal Entity Customers (2018); Appendix 1 - Beneficial Ownership (2018)

ffiec_red_flags.section: Appendix F - Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Red Flags (2014)

ofac_sls_files.section: OFAC Sanctions List Service exports (SDN + CONS_*)

items.text: Collect name, date of birth (individuals), street address (no PO boxes) and an identification number before accepting a counterparty. Numina stores only the last 4 digits of a TIN/EIN.
Verify identity using documents or non-documentary methods. Requires a licensed IDV provider; the module ships a stub that never reports 'verified'.
Keep identifying information for five years after the relationship ends; keep a record of verification methods and how discrepancies were resolved.
Understand the nature and purpose of the relationship and keep a customer risk profile (products/services, customer type, geography).
Ongoing monitoring: re-screen on list changes and when activity is inconsistent with the profile; re-screening an approved case voids its sign-off until re-approved.
For legal entities, identify each individual owning 25% or more and one control person; screen every one of them.
Screen new counterparties and their beneficial owners against current OFAC SDN and consolidated lists before accepting them or any payment.
Define name-matching criteria (fuzzy derivations) and how a hit is judged a valid match or a false hit; document every disposition.
Human cross-check of each party in OFAC Sanctions List Search, recorded on the case (not automated).
Keep lists current; record list version and sha256 on every screen; never auto-accept.

A valid match: do not proceed; escalate to counsel / OFAC hotline; blocked or rejected transactions are reported to OFAC within 10 business days (by the financial institution holding the funds; counsel to advise Numina's role).
Alert -> manage -> decide -> document. Numina is not a SAR filer; suspicious activity is documented on the payment case and escalated to counsel and, where relevant, to Stripe.
Do not tip off a counterparty that activity has been escalated or reported.
Structuring: amounts just under $10,000 or reporting/recordkeeping thresholds, alone or in clusters.
Round-dollar amounts; activity inconsistent with the customer's business or history; sudden change after dormancy.
Higher-risk jurisdictions; payments not drawn from the purchasing entity's account (payer mismatch); many payers funnelling to one payee; quick in-and-out.
Reluctance to provide ownership or business information; shell-company indicators.
No dealings with persons in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria or the Crimea, Donetsk or Luhansk regions, or with restricted-party-list persons.
No management consulting or IT consultancy services to any person located in Russia.

Public offering text contains no prohibited categories (ICOs, get-rich-quick, P2P money transmission...) and no restricted financial-services claims (treasury, crypto, lending, escrow, stored value) without Stripe approval.
Re-check the Stripe list at least every 180 days (gate fails when the recorded source date is older).
Attorney review PENDING (follow-up due 2026-12-09): blocks launch of any financial service; does not block the site push.
